purpose: Assess the 2017-2018 Laguna de Cagayan (Bangalao) Lake catch assessment as a Region II inland-water source while preserving the paper's taxonomy, aggregate sampling design, and unresolved data-quality and reuse limits.

source.title: Diversity of Fishes in Laguna de Cagayan Lake, Philippines: Status and Conservation Needs
source.author: Wilma S. Urmeneta
source.affiliation: College of Fisheries and Marine Science, Cagayan State University
source.publication: 17th World Lake Conference, Lake Kasumigaura, Ibaraki, Japan, 2018, proceedings item P1-13, printed pages 924-927
source.license: No item-specific reuse license was identified in the proceedings PDF reviewed.

studyScope.waterbody: Laguna de Cagayan Lake, also called Bangalao Lake
studyScope.administrativeLocality: Barangay Luga, Santa Teresita, Cagayan Province, Philippines
studyScope.studyPeriod: 2017-09 through 2018-03; the paper reports sampling thrice monthly, not exact dates for each sample.
sites: Site 1: Sitio Bangalao, three sampling points
Site 2: Barangay Luga, three sampling points
studyScope.samplingDescription: The study sampled fish from landing-site catches of cooperating fishers using passive fish corrals in shallow water and gill nets and hook-and-line at reported depths of 5-10 m. It says samples were randomly selected from catches of three fishers/cooperators per different fishing gear, counted and weighed, and classified to the lowest possible taxon; some were iced and transported to the COFMS-Aparri laboratory for further identification.
studyScope.localityPrecision: The paper names the lake and two study areas but does not publish station coordinates or a site-level species-by-event matrix. Do not infer coordinates from locality text or its figure.

reviewedEvidence.pooledCatch: The paper reports 1,714 fish from 14 source-labeled taxa across the lake. Reported integer counts sum to 1,714.
reviewedEvidence.siteAllocation: The paper reports 8 taxa and 186 fish at Sitio Bangalao and 14 taxa and 1,528 fish at Barangay Luga, but Table 1 does not assign individual taxa or counts to either site.
reviewedEvidence.taxonomyAndStatus: The authors say classifications were checked against FishBase 2018 and conservation labels against the 2018 IUCN Red List. Preserve these historical source labels; do not treat source-reported conservation categories or native/introduced commentary as current taxonomy or current legal status.
reviewedEvidence.sourceDataQuality: The paper's prose reports Oreochromis niloticus as 24.05% while Table 1 reports 24.50% for the same count of 420; 420/1,714 is approximately 24.50%. Other printed percentages also show small discrepancies against the integer counts. Keep the source counts and flag the percentage inconsistencies; do not infer corrected values as author-confirmed data.
reviewedEvidence.specialTaxonCaveat: The paper describes Acanthopagrus latus as one transient fish from nearby Buguey Lagoon. Preserve this as the paper's interpretation; the study does not provide an individual specimen, station, or date crosswalk for that record.

qualityAndReuseLimits: This is fishery catch evidence from cooperating fishers, not a standardized lake-wide occurrence survey. It can support a source-reported lake-level candidate checklist only; it does not establish current presence, abundance, natural range, or species-by-site occurrence.
No voucher catalog numbers, accession IDs, per-fish sample dates, species-specific station assignments, exact coordinates, or survey effort by taxon are reported in the reviewed paper.
The source uses historical taxonomy and 2018 conservation references. Current accepted names and conservation status require separate authority checks before any public projection.

No item-specific open license was found in the conference proceedings file. Do not republish the paper's table, figures, or substantial content without rights review. Publication approval remains false.
nextAction: Cross-check the 14 source labels against current taxonomic authorities while retaining the verbatim labels, and seek the author's underlying species-by-site records, sample dates, vouchers, station coordinates, and reuse terms. Continue screening independent Region II rivers, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, estuaries, and brackish waters; do not let this single lake paper stand in for province-wide or regional coverage.
